title: TWCERT/CC warns of fake short-drama apps that ask Android users for accessibility permissions
date_note: The notice gives 24 November as its publication day (updated 25 November); the page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: TWCERT/CC, the Taiwanese agency that issued the notice; pin at Taipei
summary: TWCERT/CC's notice says users who search for or click links to short-drama apps may download installers that impersonate popular apps, and attackers may also pose as Google Play or Chrome updates. It says such malicious apps may request accessibility permissions unrelated to their purpose, which could let them read screen content or act on the device remotely. The notice gives no victim figures.
plain: Taiwan's CERT warns that fake short-drama apps for Android may ask for accessibility permissions, which could let them read the screen or control the phone.
exec: Staff phones that sideload fake apps could expose personal or account data, according to TWCERT/CC's notice.
action: TWCERT/CC advises downloading apps only from official stores, denying accessibility requests unrelated to the app's function, and keeping Google Play Protect on.
impact: Awareness notice; no victim numbers given.

validation.note: Taiwan's national CERT's own notice, read in full.
